title: King Of Comedy (1983):Martin Scorsese's religious movie?

commenti.body: I don’t see this movie as much of a metaphor about religion. Sure Jerry Langford is an authority figure who Rupert admires and obsesses about, but that doesn’t make their relation resemble a religion, and certainly not the Catholic idea of religion which Martin would be most familiar about. In Martin’s actual “religious trilogy” - Kundun, Last Temptation and Silence - God is unseen and silent and works more as a great mystery rather than a shining star to be witnessed like the way Jerry Langford is portrayed. It would be more reasonable to compare Rupert to an ambitious knight loyal to a great “king”, and his love and obsession comes from his innermost desire to seize the king’s glory into his own hands.

Jerry Langford is not a true god and he can be replaced if the network says so.This is kind of reflexed to TV star making.

 I think your idea about a knight and a king is also meaningful,since the poster is a big card game.

It's just so strange to interpret Jerry's celebrity status as a metaphor for godhood: the movie title is literally The KING of Comedy, and Rupert is a lowly subject who somehow aspires to usurp his lord and become the high king.

Definitely his only movie that focuses on religion or Catholicism...

Except maybe The Last Temptation of Christ, Silence, Kundun and a major theme through lots of his body of work

I appreciate the effort you put into this post, but I don’t think there’s any examination of religion in The King of Comedy. Heck, Jerry isn’t even the most important character.  He’s certainly not the most memorable.  

Neither Jerry nor Rupert express any philosophy, doctrine or principles.  In Jerry’s world, if you can get laughs, you can be on the show.  Rupert doesn’t have that ability, doesn’t want to grind it out in the clubs, he just wants the fame and adulation.  I see Rupert as a more polished version of Travis Bickle.

I think the point is,when two intruders broke into his house,Jerry cannot yelled at him but have to keep on his humorous figure because Rupert is a big fan of his. Jerry cannot become a true man even in his house.
